description:
Send R3 a bug report about R3 ITSELF (the engine, the editor, these tools), in the user's name and naming you (your agent key or app connection). It becomes one of the user's support issues, which only the user and R3's team see. Use it when R3 does something its documentation says it should not, after checking the docs (r3_docs_read) — not for problems in the user's own project, and not for feature wishes (those are r3_roadmap_suggest).

r3_bug_reports_mine lists what the user already reported, so a fault is not filed twice. A useful report says what was done (the tool calls), what was expected and what happened, with what was MEASURED in `measurements` — the values read back with r3_component_read or r3_editor_inspect, the exact error text. `projectId` (when it happens in a project) lets R3 open it. The answer carries the report's link for the user. Rate-limited per agent key or app connection (a few an hour). Needs the support:write right.

description.description: What you did, what you expected, what happened instead.

measurements.description: What you measured: values read back, exact error text, timings. Plain text.

projectId.description: The project it happens in (r3_project_list), if any. Only a project the user can open.

title.description: One line naming the fault, e.g. "Cuboid collider with halfExtents.z = 0 inverts the contact normal".

name: r3_bug_report

answer.description: This answer in words: what was done, what R3 measured, decided or refused, and what to do next. The same text as the result's text block. Read it: the fields beside it are the data, this is the guidance.

title: File a bug report about R3
